subject: plot point color according to covariate values

messages.author: fa112d5a5313e536
messages.subject: plot point color according to covariate values
parts:
Dear List,

I would like to plot point color according to covariate values when
plotting the detection histogram and function.

Although it seems useful to be able to differentiate the detection
function for each covariate factor (for example left/right observer)
on the plot this is not a parameter which can be defined in the
plot.ds function. Maybe I am missing something here.

I have done some google search as well as looked through the
listserve. I guess there are two approaches:
- color the points according to values of the covariate on plot.ds -
currently the default is to color points as black circles, so I
thought it should be relatively simple to color according to covariate
factor...
- create smooth detection functions based on model output

There are example (incl. code) for both examples above, however non
work for me. I also see that this function is implemented in Distance2
- however, it fails for me. I have tried @Jason Roberts reworked
plot.ds2 function, see:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/detection$20covariate$20plot%7Csort:date/distance-sampling/b6pc8ytMoEw/_JxBxHxEAgAJ

but get an error message which I haven’t been able to track down:

"nrow(ddfobj$xmat)) : invalid 'times' argument which I haven’t been
able to sort out"

I have also tried Guillaume Souchay approach, but again, limited by my
R as well as statistical skills, have not succeeded - however I need
something specific for a hazardrate model / no adjustments.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/detection$20covariate$20plot%7Csort:date/distance-sampling/Xf9KnmPdXuo/o7rHPpxPBAAJ

I spend some time already to battle this one and hence was wondering
if anyone on this listserve can provide some additional code.

Looking forward to any response. Many thanks again.

Don

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] plot point color according to covariate values
parts:
Hi Don, hi listfolk,

Rather than jumping into either approach, if you simple want the dots to
be colour-coded, you can do something along the lines of the code below
(using the golf tee data shipped with mrds).

We don't have code to do this in general in Distance or mrds because
it's relly tricky once you have multiple continuous covariates in the
model. You can customise the below if you have continuous covariates by
using the quantile() function, storing the results in a column of
plotdat and then subsetting based on that.

Hopefully a forthcoming version of mrds will have a better solution,
when I can think of one.

Hope this helps in the meantime!


cheers,
--dave

---



library(mrds)
data(book.tee.data)
# fit to only observer 1 data
egdata <- book.tee.data$book.tee.dataframe
egdata <- egdata[egdata$observer==1, ]

# fit model with sex and exposure as covariates
result <- ddf(dsmodel = ~mcds(key = "hn", formula = ~sex+exposure),
data = egdata, method = "ds")

# don't plot the points
plot(result, showpoints=FALSE)

# get the data used in the model
plotdat <- result$data

# get the probabilities of detection **at a given distance** and
# store in a column of plotdat
plotdat$p <- detfct(plotdat$distance, ddfobj=result$ds$aux$ddfobj,
width=result$ds$aux$width)

## plot over the different combinations in the data
# sex=1, exposure=1
points(plotdat$distance[plotdat$sex==1 & plotdat$exposure==1],
plotdat$p[plotdat$sex==1 & plotdat$exposure==1], col="red")

# sex=0, exposure=1
points(plotdat$distance[plotdat$sex==0 & plotdat$exposure==1],
plotdat$p[plotdat$sex==0 & plotdat$exposure==1], col="green")

# sex=0, exposure=0
points(plotdat$distance[plotdat$sex==0 & plotdat$exposure==0],
plotdat$p[plotdat$sex==0 & plotdat$exposure==0], col="pink")

# sex=1, exposure=0
points(plotdat$distance[plotdat$sex==1 & plotdat$exposure==0],
plotdat$p[plotdat$sex==1 & plotdat$exposure==0], col="blue")

# make a legend
legend(2.5, 1.2, c("sex=1, exposure=1", "sex=0, exposure=1",
"sex=0, exposure=0","sex=1, exposure=0"),
c("red", "green", "pink", "blue"))
